artifacts.summary: Audit of agent-system/extensions/core/docs/ (29 files): 21 broken-link sites (dominated by a docs-README.md/README.md naming mismatch), dead /research /plan /implement command-surface references across ~13 sites, record-versioning phrasing on the dead-command topic, a stale component inventory (fork-patterns.md undiscoverable), 3 duplication instances with recommended single authorities (command syntax, Three-Layer Architecture, extension-picker link sites), and explicit deferral flags for the two sites that touch the 8-record scope boundary.

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/docs/, the hub file is docs-README.md, not README.md (no plain README.md exists at that level). Many files' breadcrumb links read [Back to Docs](../README.md), which is broken in both the source store and the deployed .claude/docs/ tree (deploy never renames it). Any future docs audit in this repo should check for this specific mismatch first.

lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh only catches the literal 'Next:'/'Run /X' recommendation shape. A much larger population of dead /research, /plan, /implement command-surface references survives in tables, ASCII diagrams, and prose examples that never match that shape. A clean lint run does not mean a corpus is free of dead-command references; a broader grep across tables/prose is needed too.

When a research/audit task carries an explicit scope boundary naming other open records as substantive owners of specific files, the right move at structural-fix sites inside those files is to classify each site as 'safe to fix' (illustrative example data, naming-only) vs. 'flag for deferral' (touches what the field/consumer actually asserts) rather than either deciding the substance or refusing to touch the file at all.
